intro.en: Aleph. The first letter, the number one, the breath before every word.
intro.src: The first of the three mother letters

lines.en: Look closely: an aleph is drawn from three letters. A yod above, a yod below, and a vav between them.
Yod, vav, yod: 10 + 6 + 10 = 26, the number of God's four-letter Name, hidden inside the first letter.
The upper yod is the waters above, the lower yod the waters below, the vav the sky between them.
lines.src: Genesis 1:7, as the mystics read it

lines.en: Aleph makes no sound of its own. It is the open breath that every vowel rides on.
Aleph was made king over air: the sky in the world, the mild season in the year, the chest in the body.
Some sages taught that at Sinai the people heard only the aleph of Anochi, "I am": a silence holding every word.
Echad, one, begins with aleph. In the Zohar God tells it: my oneness is known only through you.
Turn aleph around and read it backwards: אלף becomes פלא, pele. Wonder.
In the oldest Hebrew script aleph was an ox's head, horns and all: the strength that pulls the plough.
The same three letters spell aluf, master; elef, a thousand; and a'alefcha, I will teach you.
Three mother letters: aleph, mem, shin. Air, water, fire. Aleph is the air between, keeping fire and water in balance.
Aleph is one. Spelled in full, אלף adds to 111: one, ten, a hundred. One at every level.
Every letter asked to begin the world. Aleph alone held back, and was promised the first word at Sinai.

intro.en: Bet. The second letter, the number two, the house: the Torah opens with it.

lines.en: Why does the Torah begin with bet? It is closed on three sides and open only forward: do not ask what is above or behind, begin from here.
In the beginning: the first word of the Torah opens with a bet, not an aleph.
The world opens with bet because bet is the language of blessing, berakhah.
Bet is two. Two are better than one: if one falls, the other lifts them up.
With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it stands.
Make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.
Where does God live? Wherever we let God in.
Bet is bayit, a house: a roof, a floor and a back wall, with the front left open for whoever comes.

intro.en: Gimel. The third letter, the number three: gamal, the camel, and gomel, the one who gives.

lines.en: Gimel, dalet: gemol dalim, be kind to the poor.

lines.he: דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים לִרְדּוֹף אַחַר דַּלִּים
lines.en: Why does the gimel's foot reach toward the dalet? It is the way of the kind to run after those in need.
The world stands on three things: Torah, prayer and acts of kindness.
A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
Gimel is the camel, carrying water and bread across the desert to whoever is waiting at the other side.
On the dreidel, gimel stands for gadol: a great miracle happened there.
The world is built on kindness.
Kindness is greater than charity: it gives with your body, not only your money, to the rich and the poor, the living and the dead.

intro.en: Dalet. The fourth letter, the number four: delet, a door, and dal, the one who has little.

lines.en: Why does the dalet's foot reach back toward the gimel? So the one in need is easy to find.
And why does the dalet turn its face away? So the gift is given in secret, and no one is shamed.
From the four corners of the earth.

lines.he: פִּתְחוּ לִי פֶּתַח כְּחֻדּוֹ שֶׁל מַחַט
lines.en: Open for Me a door as small as the eye of a needle, and I will open for you a door wide enough for wagons.
A broken and humbled heart, God will not turn away.
Lift up your heads, O gates, and let the King of glory come in.
Open for me the gates of justice; I will go in and give thanks.
Dalet bends at the top like someone bowing: humility is the door a blessing comes through.

intro.en: Heh. The fifth letter, the number five, the sound of breath leaving the body.

lines.en: When they were created, be-hibar'am, can be read be-heh bera'am: with heh He created them.
Every letter takes hold of the tongue except heh. So the world was made with no toil, only a breath.
Why is the world shaped like a heh? It is open below: whoever wants to leave may leave.
And why does its leg hang free, leaving a gap above? So whoever turns back can come in again, from above.
God added a heh to Abram and to Sarai, and they became Abraham and Sarah.
Let every breath praise God.
The breath of every living thing blesses Your name.

intro.en: Kaf. The eleventh letter, the number twenty: kaf, the palm of the hand.
intro.src: One of the seven double letters

lines.en: Kaf is the palm: open to give, cupped to receive. The same hand does both.
Kaf begins keter, the crown: the highest of the ten sefirot, above even wisdom.
Three crowns: of Torah, of priesthood, of kingship. The crown of a good name rises above them all.
All you peoples, clap your hands, tik’u chaf. Shout to God with a voice of joy.
Nesiat kapayim, the lifting of the palms: the priests raise both hands to bless the people.
Kaf is a double: with a point inside it is k, without it kh. A strong sound and a gentle one.
The bent kaf and the straight one at a word’s end: one who bows in this world will stand upright in the next.
As a prefix, kaf means like. It is the letter of likeness.

intro.en: Mem. The mother letter of water, the hum of closed lips, the number forty.
intro.src: The second of the three mother letters

lines.en: A song of ascents: from the depths I call to You. The climb begins at the bottom, in the deep water.
As water gives a face back to a face, so one heart answers another.
Mem is forty: forty days of rain, forty days on the mountain, forty years in the desert, forty measures of water in a mikveh.
In the oldest Hebrew script mem was drawn as a line of waves. It is named for water, mayim.
Mem hums with the lips closed, shin hisses, and aleph is the breath that keeps the balance between them.
Ho, all who are thirsty, come to the water. The sages read it: there is no water but Torah.
Mem was made king over water: the earth in the world, the cold season in the year, the belly in the body.
Mem has two forms, open מ and closed ם. The sages said: an open teaching and a hidden one.
Emet, truth: aleph from the start of the letters, mem from the middle, tav from the end. Truth is the seal of God.
Shamayim, the heavens, were made of fire and water mixed together: esh and mayim, shin and mem.

intro.en: Peh. The seventeenth letter, the number eighty: peh, the mouth.
intro.src: One of the seven double letters

lines.en: Peh is the mouth. Where the Torah says a living soul, the old translation says a speaking spirit.
Pesach is peh sach, the mouth speaks: the exodus freed the voice of a people who could not speak.
Look into the peh: the white space in its mouth is the shape of a bet, the first letter of the Torah, hidden in speech.
Silence is a fence around wisdom.
The open peh and the closed one: a time to keep silent and a time to speak.
Peh is a double: with a point inside it is p, without it f. Hard and soft, the same mouth.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue.
Peh is eighty, and eighty is the age of gevurah, strength.

intro.en: Resh. The twentieth letter, the number two hundred: rosh, the head, and reshit, the beginning.
intro.src: One of the seven double letters

lines.en: Dalet and resh differ by one small corner. In the Shema the dalet of echad, one, is written large, so it is never read as acher, another.
The corner that makes a dalet is a yod. Without that point, the same shape is a resh.
Resh is rosh, the head: what leads, and what the rest follows.
Bereshit, in the beginning, carries reshit inside it: the beginning, the head, the first.
Rashi reads in the beginning as for the sake of the beginning: the Torah and Israel, both called reshit.
Kuf and resh: kadosh and rasha, holy and wicked. The kuf turns its face away, yet leaves its leg open for the one who comes back.
Resh is counted among the seven doubles, though few still say its second sound.

intro.en: Shin. The mother letter of fire, the hiss of the flame, three heads rising from one root.
intro.src: The third of the three mother letters

lines.en: Moses saw a bush burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
The soul of a person is the lamp of God. Like a flame, it reaches up.
On the tefillin worn on the head a shin is pressed into the leather on both sides: three heads on one side, four on the other.
Three heads rising from one root: the mystics see in them the three fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Love is as strong as death. Its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of God.
Shin hisses like a flame, mem hums like water, and aleph is the breath between them.
Shamayim, the heavens, were made of fire and water mixed together: esh and mayim.
Shin was made king over fire: the heavens in the world, the heat in the year, the head in the body.
Man and woman, ish and ishah, share the letters of esh, fire. What keeps it from consuming them is God's Name between them, yod and heh.
Shaddai, the Name written on the outside of every mezuzah, begins with shin.
Shema, Shabbat, shalom: the words at the heart of a Jewish day all begin with shin.

intro.en: Tav. The last letter, the number four hundred: a mark, a sign, a seal.
intro.src: The last of the seven double letters

lines.en: The seal of the Holy One is emet, truth.
Tav means a mark. Ezekiel saw a tav set on the foreheads of those who grieved for the city.
Emet, truth: aleph the first letter, mem the middle, tav the last. Truth holds from beginning to end.
The Torah’s first sentence holds a word that is only aleph and tav: et. The mystics read it as every letter, first to last.
Their end is wedged in their beginning, and their beginning in their end.
Tav is the last double: t with the point inside, th without. Some communities still say the soft tav.
Tav is four hundred, the largest number a single letter carries: the count of the alef-bet ends here.
